newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway PM votes for economy, health, environment.
newsitem.headline: Norway PM votes for economy, health, environment.

text.p: Norwegian Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland said on Monday that he would fight parliamentary elections in September on accountability for the economy, health and the environment.
Speaking at his annual summer news conference, Jagland accused opposition parties of irresponsibility over "a carousel" of overspending during negotiations for the revised 1997 budget.

The Labour minority government came under pressure in the June budget debate from opposition centrist parties and the far right, who had argued public spending should be raised by around eight billion crowns ($1.1 billion).

"It is discouraging to see that as soon as the country has overcome the (economic) troubles, the government is met with the largest overbidding proposal in history," said Jagland, who succeeded veteran premier Gro Harlem Brundtland last October.
There had been "overbidding both when it comes to increased spending and overbidding when it comes to cutting taxes", he added.

Norwegians will go to the polls on September 15 and recent opinion polls have indicated a slide in support for the ruling Labour Party. Business and financial markets, however, favour Labour's stance on keeping spending under control.
The three centrist parties -- the Christian People's Party, the Centre Party and liberal Venstre -- have said they will raise spending if they gain enough votes to form a coalition government.

They want to invest more of Norway's oil wealth in schools and public transport while the Labour government is setting aside the budget surplus -- projected at 57.3 billion crowns this year -- in the State Petroleum Fund for investment overseas.

A mid-June opinion poll published by the daily Aftenposten, showed the Labour Party, which won 36.9 percent of the votes in the 1993 election, with 30.6 percent of voter support. The poll put the total for the three centrist parties at 28.8 percent.

"We will make it an election on responsibility for the economy, health and the environment," Jagland said, adding that "responsible economic politics" meant low inflation, low interest rates and battling unemployment.
The premier repeated the Labour Party's threat used in the 1993 election that the government would resign if it failed to get sufficient support in parliament for its policies.
"If it is not possible to have a continued policy for fighting unemployment and keeping low interest rates and low inflation, then we cannot continue," he said.
"Before the election in 1993 we said we could not continue unless we got support for policies that would reduce unemployment. We are saying the same thing now." ($ = 7.292 Norwegian Crowns)
